description: Inputs for capacity_model.py. Every leaf that matters is {v, basis, note}. basis is one of: CODE (read from Rider_UAM source/config defaults), ASSUMPTION (a judgement, not measured, change it), USER (stated by the product owner), PLACEHOLDER (must be replaced by a measurement from ops/loadtest before the output is used for sizing), MEASUREMENT (a value copied from a filled ops/loadtest/results-template.md; none exist yet). As committed, nothing in this file is a measurement.

daily_active_pct_low.note: Daily active share of registered users, low end (3.0M DAU).

daily_active_pct_high.note: Daily active share of registered users, high end (4.0M DAU).

registration_growth_pct_per_year.note: New accounts per year as a percentage of the current base.

ever_logged_in_pct.note: Share of registered users that have at least one session/device/login-security row.

devices_per_logged_in_user.note: user_devices rows per user that has logged in (one per distinct User-Agent fingerprint).

peak_active_pct.note: Low end of the stated 10-20% busiest-window range (1.0M of 10M).
Midpoint of the stated range (1.5M). The midpoint is our choice, not a forecast.
High end of the stated range (2.0M).

login_fraction.note: Share of the active users that perform a FULL login (password/OTP) inside the window. The rest hold a 30-day refresh token and only refresh. Unknown: depends on client behaviour and whether the peak coincides with a start-of-day login wave.
Share of the active users that perform a full login inside the 15-minute burst (a login storm, e.g. a push notification or a shift change).

refresh_participation.note: Fraction of active users whose client keeps the session alive by refreshing once per access-token lifetime (refreshes in window = minutes / access_ttl_minutes x participation).

me_privileges_per_hour.note: GET /identity/me/privileges. Rider_Web calls it at app load; mobile apps were not found to call it. 0.6 = 'about 60% of active users load a web screen in an hour'.

me_organizations_per_hour.note: GET /identity/me/organizations, called with the privilege fetch by Rider_Web (organization switcher).

user_lookup_per_hour.note: Service-to-service reads of UAM (GET /users/{id}, /users/by-phone, /users/batch, /directory/users) per active user per hour. The gateway does NOT call UAM per request (see capacity-model.md section 2), so this is only other services' lookups.

active_staff_in_window.note: Back-office users active in the window; they use the user list and search screens.

intra_window_peak_factor.note: Busiest second inside the window as a multiple of the window average. 1.0 = perfectly flat arrivals.

access_ttl_minutes.note: JWT lifetime. Default of UAM_JWT_EXPIRY_MINUTES; a deployment may override it.

bcrypt_strength.note: bcrypt cost factor; each +1 doubles the CPU cost of a login.

hash_pool_queue_capacity.note: Logins that may wait for a free bcrypt worker before new ones get 503.

hash_timeout_ms.note: A login that cannot get its bcrypt result in this time gets 503.

login_cpu_ms.note: CPU milliseconds of one full login (bcrypt + session/token/audit writes). The code comment in PasswordService says ~202 ms per bcrypt op at strength 11 on 'reference hardware'; that is a claim in the repo, not a measurement on your hardware. Replace with the measured value (results-template.md).

other_cpu_ms.note: CPU milliseconds of every non-login request on average (JWT parse, JSON, one or two queries). Replace with a measured value.

login.note: Total time a pooled connection is held per login across its roughly 20 statements (code review: user x3 lookups, lockout x2, credential, mfa, membership, tenant, application access, device, session, refresh token, login security, 2 audit inserts). Measure with pg_stat_statements / Hikari metrics.

refresh.note: Connection hold per refresh (token, user, membership, tenant, app access, 2 token writes, session update).

me_privileges.note: Connection hold per privilege fetch (user, one role per role code, permissions IN).

user_list.note: Connection hold per paged user list at 10M rows. Includes the count(*) the Page query runs, which on 10M rows is a scan; dominated by that.

user_search.note: Connection hold per free-text user search at 10M rows (LIKE '%x%' over 7 columns cannot use a b-tree index, plus count). Order of seconds is expected until a trigram index or search service is used.

cores.note: CPU cores (limit) per UAM pod; the bcrypt worker pool is sized to availableProcessors().

cpu_target_utilization.note: Fraction of the CPU you accept to run at in the peak (rest is headroom for GC, spikes, a lost pod).

headroom.note: Used in required_instances = ceil(rps / (sustainable_rps_per_instance x (1 - headroom))).

sustainable_rps_per_instance.note: REPLACE with the rps at breakpoint from ops/loadtest/breakpoint.js on ONE instance sized like production (results-template.md). Leave null to print the table below only.

max_connections.note: Postgres max_connections of the real server (PostgreSQL's own default is 100).

connections_reserved_for_others.note: Connections used by the gateway, other services, admin sessions, replication and superuser_reserved_connections.

usable_fraction.note: Never plan to use more than this fraction of the connections left for UAM.

ram_gb.note: RAM of the database host, for the working-set comparison.

requests_per_active_user_per_hour.note: Requests an active user sends through the gateway per hour (all services).

logins_per_dau_per_day.note: Full logins per daily active user per day.

active_minutes_per_dau_per_day.note: Minutes a DAU keeps the app open; refreshes per day = this / access_ttl_minutes.

failed_attempts_per_dau_per_day.note: Failed login attempts (typos, bots) per DAU per day.

tables.name: uam_users
tables.note: index_bytes: pk + user_name + email + phone_e164 + V15 upper(user_name), upper(email), number.

tables.name: password_history
tables.note: one row at registration, one per password change.

tables.name: user_login_security
tables.note: one per user that has logged in; updated on every login (hot row per user).

tables.name: user_devices
tables.note: one per user and User-Agent fingerprint.

tables.name: user_sessions
tables.note: one per full login, never deleted by the current code (no cleanup job found).

tables.name: refresh_tokens
tables.note: one per login AND one per refresh (rotation inserts a new row, marks the old revoked); never deleted by the current code.

tables.name: audit_logs
tables.note: one per login success/failure from the auth path; admin actions add more (not counted).

tables.name: uam_auth_audit_events
tables.note: one per login success/failure/lockout; never deleted by the current code.

tables.name: uam_login_attempts
tables.note: one row per failed identifier; an expired row is deleted only when the same identifier tries again, so it effectively accumulates. retention_days here is the lockout window, NOT an implemented purge.

proposed_retention_days.note: Used for the 'with retention' column. No purge job exists in UAM today, so the 'unbounded' column is the current behaviour.

loadtest.note: Weights used by ops/loadtest/mixed-peak.js (they must add to 100). They are the endpoint shares printed by capacity_model.py for the 'expected' scenario, peak_hour window, rounded; capacity_model.py warns if they drift more than 2 points from its own output.
